title: FKG positive-cone closure and compact-upper-set sum in the tempered topology
question: Are the closed-cone and translation-invariant-metric hypotheses used by the continuous-loop FKG Borel extension valid for the actual projective tempered topology?
method: Read the declared metric d_t and projective space in manuscript.tex.
Prove closure of the pointwise nonnegative cone using the local sup components of d_t.
Prove compact-plus-closed-cone sums are closed and upper using compact subsequences and translation invariance.
Insert the proof as a labeled manuscript lemma and retain the external-review boundary.
finding: The actual d_t topology contains local sup convergence at each site, so the pointwise positive cone is closed. The metric is translation invariant, and compactness of K plus closedness of the cone proves K+E_+ is closed; upperness follows by addition. The manuscript now states and proves this as Lemma lem:positive-cone-topology before the Borel FKG extension.
decision_reason: The repair removes an implicit topological premise from the FKG passage without changing the finite log-supermodularity, weak-limit, DLR, cusp or state claims. It is a local proof repair and still requires independent review of the surrounding FKG argument.
boundary: T0 internal topological sublemma; no claim tier, theorem promotion, TECT sector, or PDF status change.
next_action: Re-run the manuscript and integrated audits, then obtain a signed review of the complete continuous-loop FKG and selected-limit passage.
non_claims: This does not certify the continuous-loop FKG theorem or phase coexistence.
It does not prove the DLR tangent, infrared, cusp or parity-state conclusion.
No KMS, ground-state, continuum, cosmology, Sector A or publication conclusion changes.
